Custom Kitchen Cabinets In San Antonio

C&S Remodeling handles cabinet-only projects, cabinet refacing, and replacement cabinetry in San Antonio, as well as cabinets within a full kitchen remodel. Our veteran-owned and woman-owned team helps you choose the right scope for your kitchen. Cabinet lead time is typically 2–6 weeks; confirm your selections and installation schedule during your consultation.

CONTACT US
About Our Kitchen Cabinet Services

Our kitchen remodelers offer top-tier kitchen cabinet services to transform your kitchen into a stylish and functional space. We provide cabinet services made to meet your unique needs and preferences. Whether you're looking to update your current cabinetry with a fresh, modern look or want to install completely new, high-end cabinets, our experienced team ensures a seamless process from design to cabinet installation.

‍Using only the finest materials, C&S Remodeling guarantees durability and aesthetic appeal, enhancing the overall value and beauty of your kitchen.

Kitchen Cabinet Styles For Every San Antonio Home

Your cabinet style sets the tone for your entire kitchen. Our design team helps you select the perfect style to complement your home's architecture and your personal taste.

Shaker Style Cabinets

The most popular choice in San Antonio and across the country, Shaker cabinets feature a five-piece door with a recessed center panel and clean, simple lines. This versatile style works beautifully in traditional, transitional, and even contemporary kitchens. Available in every finish from crisp white to rich espresso, Shaker cabinets offer timeless appeal that won't look dated in 10 or 20 years.

Flat-Panel (Slab) Cabinets

Sleek and modern, flat-panel doors have no frames or raised panels—just a smooth, uninterrupted surface. This minimalist style is perfect for contemporary and modern kitchens where clean lines take priority. High-gloss finishes make a bold statement, while matte finishes offer understated sophistication.

Raised Panel Cabinets

The hallmark of traditional kitchen design, raised panel doors feature a center panel that projects outward from the frame. Ornate profiles and detailed moldings create a classic, elegant look that pairs beautifully with San Antonio's many traditional and Spanish-influenced homes.

Glass-Front Cabinets

Add visual interest and display your favorite dishware with glass-front cabinets. Options range from clear glass to seeded, frosted, or leaded glass. Glass fronts work as accent pieces—typically installed in select upper cabinets—to break up solid door expanses and add depth to your design.

Open Shelving

Increasingly popular in modern and farmhouse kitchens, open shelving replaces some or all upper cabinets with floating shelves. This approach creates an open, airy feel and puts everyday items within easy reach. Our designers can help you balance open shelving with closed storage for practical functionality.

CONTACT US
Custom Cabinet Options For Your Home

If you want new cabinets, our team can help you design, build, and install the perfect setup in your home. During the design phase, we customize our approach depending on your kitchen's dimensions. Whether you have a cozy kitchen or tons of space, we'll find a solution that suits you. Extensive experience lets us avoid common mistakes like overcrowding, inadequate storage, or ignoring the work triangle. Our kitchen cabinet installation company can enhance your home value with custom design, including elements like:

Cabinet Styles


Choose from Shaker, flat-panel, glass-front, raised, or other panel options for a traditional or sleek appearance.

Materials


If you want natural wood, we can discuss various types to find your desired look.

Finishes


Options include solid paint colors or different shades of wood stains. If you choose paint, you can customize everything from glossy to matte finishes.

Hardware


Select knobs and pulls in various styles, metals, and finishes. We can also discuss internal hardware like soft-close hinges.

Functionality


Add elements that suit your daily life, like pull-out shelves, spice racks, drawer dividers, and corner cabinets.

Specialty Cabinets


Create more storage space with expansive pantries or conceal the clutter with appliance garages.

Decorative Elements


Crown molding, trim, or under-cabinet lighting can add an extra touch of elegance that elevates your space.

Should You Reface Or Replace Your Kitchen Cabinets?

If your existing cabinet boxes are in good condition, refacing can deliver a dramatic transformation at a lower cost than full replacement. For the broader project budget, compare refresh and full-remodel budgets in our kitchen cost guide. Here's how to decide:

‍

Consider Cabinet Refacing If:
Your cabinet boxes are structurally sound (no warping, water damage, or loose joints)
You're happy with your current kitchen layout
Your cabinets are solid wood or quality plywood construction
You want to change the style or color without major disruption
Budget is a primary concern (refacing typically costs 40-50% less than replacement)

‍

Consider New Custom Cabinets If:
Your cabinet boxes show signs of damage, warping, or moisture issues
You want to change your kitchen layout or add storage
Current cabinets are particle board or low-quality construction
You're doing a complete kitchen remodel with layout changes
Your current cabinets are poorly designed or inefficiently laid out

‍

Not sure which option is right for you? Our design team can assess your existing cabinets and provide honest recommendations based on their condition and your goals.

Understanding Cabinet Construction And Materials

Not all cabinets are created equal. Understanding construction methods and materials helps you make informed decisions about quality and value.

Cabinet Box Construction

‍

Plywood Construction (Recommended)

The gold standard for cabinet boxes. Plywood is made from thin layers of wood veneer glued together, creating a strong, stable material that resists warping and holds screws securely. Our custom cabinets feature plywood box construction for lasting durability.

‍

Particle Board

Made from wood particles bonded with resin, particle board is less expensive but more susceptible to moisture damage and doesn't hold hardware as well over time. Common in builder-grade and budget cabinets.

‍

MDF (Medium-Density Fiberboard)

Engineered wood that's denser and smoother than particle board. MDF is excellent for painted doors due to its smooth surface, but performs poorly when exposed to moisture.

Door Materials

‍

Solid Wood

Premium choice for natural beauty and durability. Solid wood doors can be stained to showcase grain patterns or painted for a smooth finish. Species options include maple, cherry, oak, hickory, and more, each with unique characteristics.

‍

MDF with Wood Veneer

MDF core with a thin layer of real wood veneer offers the look of solid wood at a lower price point. An excellent choice for stained finishes when budget is a consideration.

‍

Thermofoil

Vinyl film applied over MDF creates a smooth, easy-clean surface at a budget-friendly price. Best for painted looks, though it can peel over time with heat exposure near ovens and dishwashers.

Custom Storage Solutions For Your Kitchen

Modern cabinet design goes far beyond doors and drawers. We incorporate intelligent storage solutions that maximize every inch of your kitchen and make daily life easier.

Pull-Out Shelves


Transform deep base cabinets from black holes into easily accessible storage. Pull-out shelves bring items from the back of the cabinet right to you—no more kneeling and reaching into dark corners.

Corner Cabinet Solutions


Don't waste valuable corner space. Lazy Susans, pull-out corner units, and magic corner systems make the most of these challenging areas, keeping pots, pans, and appliances organized and accessible.

Appliance Garages


Keep countertops clear while keeping frequently-used appliances accessible. Appliance garages hide blenders, toasters, and coffee makers behind a door that lifts or slides away when needed.

Drawer Organizers


Custom-fitted drawer inserts keep utensils, spices, and tools neatly organized. Options include knife blocks, spice drawer inserts, and adjustable dividers that adapt to your specific needs.

Vertical Storage


Narrow pull-outs beside the range store cooking oils and spices at arm's reach. Tall pantry pull-outs maximize vertical space while keeping everything visible and organized.

Waste And Recycling Centers


Built-in pull-out bins for trash and recycling keep waste out of sight and make sorting convenient. Multiple compartment options accommodate San Antonio's recycling programs.

Our Step-By-Step Kitchen Cabinet Process

We follow a structured, step-by-step process to create customized 3D renderings of your kitchen for your remodel. Whether you're just exploring possibilities or ready to dive into construction, our approach ensures a smooth and enjoyable experience.

01.
Initial Consultation & Design

The kitchen cabinet installation process at C&S Remodeling begins with an in-depth initial consultation. You meet with a design specialist during this phase to discuss your vision, needs, and preferences. This step is crucial as it allows our team to understand the specific requirements and style preferences.

We will take measurements, assess the kitchen layout, and offer expert advice on cabinet styles, materials, and finishes. By the end of the consultation, we will have created a detailed cabinet design plan that aligns every aspect of the project with your expectations.

02.
Cabinet Selection

After the design approval, the process moves into selecting the perfect cabinets for your kitchen. C&S Remodeling offers a wide range of high-quality materials and styles, ensuring each piece meets your aesthetic and functional needs. Our team provides expert guidance to help you select cabinets that enhance your kitchen's look and durability. With a focus on precision and detail, we make sure your cabinets are beautiful and built to last, perfectly fitting your kitchen's specific dimensions and style.

03.
Professional Cabinet Installation

Once the cabinets are selected, the professional installation phase begins. Our kitchen cabinet installers at C&S Remodeling handle each project with care and efficiency. They provide secure and accurate cabinet installation, paying close attention to alignment and functionality. We complete this step promptly with minimal disruption to the household. The result is a seamlessly integrated kitchen cabinet system that enhances the overall look and usability of the space.

04.
Final Inspection And Client Approval

The final step in our kitchen cabinet installation process is the thorough inspection and client approval. After installation, we conduct a detailed inspection to make sure every kitchen cabinet is perfectly installed and meets the highest quality standards. The team checks for proper alignment, finishes, and functionality, addressing any minor adjustments if necessary.

Once the inspection is complete, we invite you to review the work. That way, you can be sure you are completely satisfied with the outcome. Then, we make any final touches to achieve perfection. We only consider the project complete when you are happy with your new kitchen cabinets.

Get Inspired By Past Projects

We have thrilled many homeowners with the results of our kitchen remodel projects. Check out our portfolio if you want ideas for your project or want to see our capabilities. Our past work shows how we have created stunning cabinet designs and performed professional kitchen cabinet installation in San Antonio and surrounding areas. These previous projects showcase our expertise, from classic natural wood to minimalist designs with understated hardware.

Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Cabinets
How Long Does Cabinet Installation Take?


Cabinet lead time is typically 2–6 weeks. Installation is scheduled separately after the cabinets arrive and generally takes 2–4 days for a complete replacement in an average-sized kitchen. Confirm the schedule for your cabinet selection and project scope during your consultation.

Can You Match My Existing Cabinets For An Addition Or Island?


We'll do our best to match your existing cabinets. If an exact match isn't possible, our designers can recommend complementary options that coordinate beautifully—like a contrasting island color that intentionally stands out.

What's The Best Cabinet Finish For San Antonio's Climate?


San Antonio's humidity can affect wood cabinets. We recommend quality finishes with proper sealing, and for painted cabinets, conversion varnishes that resist moisture and yellowing. Our team specifies finishes appropriate for Texas conditions.

Do You Remove And Dispose Of Old Cabinets?


Yes, cabinet removal and disposal is included in our full-service cabinet installation. We handle everything so you don't have to coordinate multiple contractors or haul debris yourself.

Custom Kitchen Countertops In San Antonio

C&S Remodeling includes custom kitchen countertops in larger kitchen remodeling projects in San Antonio. We're veteran-owned, woman-owned, and family-run, serving homeowners since 2015. We don't take standalone countertop replacement jobs. Our team helps you choose surfaces that work with your cabinets, layout, and overall remodeling budget, with options including granite, quartz, marble, and quartzite. Kitchen remodeling projects include complimentary 3D renderings so you can review countertop choices alongside your cabinets, flooring, and lighting before construction.

CONTACT US
About Our Kitchen Countertop Installation Experts

C&S Remodeling includes countertop selection and installation as part of larger kitchen remodels throughout San Antonio. Our team specializes in granite, quartz, marble, and other premium surfaces, ensuring each kitchen countertop is crafted and installed precisely and carefully. Whether you want the durability of quartz, the look of marble, or the unique patterns of granite, at C&S Remodeling, our services meet your specific needs and style preferences.

See your new kitchen countertops before work even begins with our AI Visualizer Tool. Explore different counter top styles and colors!

Countertop Materials We Install
Granite Countertops


Granite is the most popular kitchen countertop material in San Antonio for good reason. It's durable, heat-resistant, and every slab is one of a kind. Because granite is quarried from natural stone, no two countertops will look identical, which is part of the appeal for homeowners who want a kitchen that doesn't look like every other kitchen on the block. We help you pick from a wide range of color families (classic blacks and grays, or dramatic blues, golds, and reds), and we'll bring slab samples to your home so you can see how each one looks in your actual lighting before you commit.

Granite needs to be sealed periodically to keep it stain-resistant, and we'll walk you through the maintenance basics during the final review.

Marble Countertops


Marble is the look most clients picture when they think "luxury kitchen": soft veining, a cool surface, the kind of finish that ages into something with character. It's also the most demanding material on this list. Marble etches when it meets acidic foods like lemon juice or wine, and it stains more easily than granite or quartz. We're upfront about that during your consultation because marble is a great fit for some kitchens and the wrong choice for others. If you love the look but cook with citrus daily, we'll often steer you toward a quartz that mimics marble veining instead. Same aesthetic, none of the upkeep.

Other Surfaces — Butcher Block, Concrete, And Solid Surface


For clients who want something outside the stone family, we also install butcher block (warm, food-safe, needs oiling), concrete (custom-poured, industrial look, can be tinted or stamped), and solid surface options like Corian. We don't push these. Most kitchens we remodel land on granite or quartz, but if you're going for a specific aesthetic, we'll make it work.

Quartz Countertops


Quartz is our most-requested countertop material in San Antonio, especially for homeowners with kids, frequent dinner parties, or busy weeknights. Unlike granite, quartz is engineered (natural quartz crystals bonded with resin), so it's non-porous, stain-resistant, and never needs sealing. The pattern stays consistent slab to slab, which makes it easy to predict how the finished kitchen will look. Quartz also comes in finishes that mimic high-end marble without the maintenance, which is why we install so much of it in San Antonio remodels.

We work with all the major quartz brands and will help you compare warranties, finishes, and price tiers so you're not paying for a name when a comparable option costs less.

Quartzite Countertops


Quartzite is the material clients land on when they want the look of marble with the durability of granite. It's a natural stone (not the same as quartz) that's harder than granite, doesn't etch the way marble does, and shows the kind of dramatic veining that turns a countertop into the focal point of the kitchen. Pricing sits at the higher end, and supply varies by slab, so we'll help you check inventory before we lock in a design.

Kitchen Countertop Cost In San Antonio

Kitchen countertop pricing in San Antonio varies more than most homeowners expect, because the slab itself is only part of the cost. The biggest variables are square footage, material grade, edge profile complexity, cutout count (sinks, cooktops, faucets), and whether your existing layout needs structural work to accept the new surface. Countertops are priced within the scope of your larger kitchen remodel. C&S kitchen projects range from roughly $25,000 for a small kitchen to $85,000, depending on scope and size; this is the overall kitchen budget, not a countertop-only price.  We don't quote pricing without seeing your kitchen. After your in-home consultation, you'll get an itemized estimate that breaks down material, fabrication, removal of the old countertops, plumbing reconnection, and any add-on work, so you know what you're paying for line by line. Countertops are included as part of a larger kitchen project. Use our guide to plan your overall kitchen remodel budget.

Our Testimonials
Are You Ready To Create Your New Space?
Book Appointment
Why Choose C&S Remodeling For Your Kitchen Countertops?
Veteran-Owned, Woman-Owned, Family-Run

C&S Remodeling was founded in 2015 by Scott and Carol. Scott brings a military and IT background, Carol brings the design eye, and both of them are personally involved in every project. We're one of the few veteran-owned and woman-owned remodeling companies in San Antonio, and we built the company on the belief that you should know exactly who's working in your kitchen and who to call when you have a question. No call centers, no project handoffs.

Design-Build, All Under One Roof

Countertops are one part of the larger kitchen projects C&S handles. Our design-build team plans the cabinets, surfaces, layout, plumbing, electrical work, and finishes together so countertop choices fit the complete remodel. We don't offer standalone countertop fabrication or replacement.

Complimentary 3D Renderings

Before installation, we produce a full 3D rendering of your new kitchen so you can see how your chosen countertop looks alongside your cabinets, backsplash, flooring, and lighting. You can swap materials, change edge profiles, and adjust colors in the rendering, not after installation when changes are expensive. Every kitchen remodeling project at C&S includes this rendering at no extra charge.

Honest Material Guidance

We'll tell you when a material is wrong for your kitchen. If you cook with citrus and want marble, we'll show you a quartz that nails the look without the maintenance. If you want the absolute best stain resistance, we'll point you to quartz over granite. Our job is to make sure you're happy with your countertops in five years, not just at the install walkthrough.

Our Countertop Installation Process

We've built our installation process around removing the surprises that derail most kitchen remodels in San Antonio. Here's exactly what to expect from your first call to the final walkthrough.

1. In-Home Consultation And Material Selection


We come to your home, look at your existing kitchen, and talk through what you're trying to accomplish, whether that's matching a recently updated cabinet color, opening up a tight galley layout, or finally fixing a counter that's been bothering you for years. We'll bring slab samples in the materials you're considering so you can see them under your kitchen's actual lighting. By the end of this visit, you'll have a clear sense of which material fits your budget, your habits, and the look you want.

2. Precise Measurement And 3D Rendering


Our team uses laser-precise measurements rather than tape-and-pencil to capture every cabinet, overhang, and seam location. Those measurements feed into a full 3D rendering of your new kitchen (countertops, cabinets, backsplash, and lighting) so you can review the design before fabrication starts. If something looks off in the rendering, we change it. Once you approve, we move to fabrication.

3. Fabrication And Installation


We disconnect plumbing and electrical, remove the existing countertops carefully to protect your cabinets and floors, and bring the new slabs in. Our installers level, scribe, and seam them with the kind of attention you'd expect from a craftsman who's about to be on this same job tomorrow. Sinks get re-mounted, faucets reinstalled, garbage disposals reconnected. You don't end up with a dish you can't run.

4. Final Walkthrough And Care Guidance


Before we leave, we walk through every edge, seam, and surface with you. We'll explain the maintenance routine for your specific material (how often to seal granite, how to clean quartz, what to keep off marble) and answer any final questions. If anything isn't right, we fix it before we pack up.

Frequently Asked Questions
How Long Does A Kitchen Countertop Installation Take In San Antonio?


Most kitchen countertop installations finish in one day once the slabs are fabricated and on site. Templating happens during the design phase, fabrication typically takes 7–14 business days depending on material availability, and installation itself is a single visit. You'll be without a working kitchen sink for roughly 24 hours on install day.

What's The Most Durable Countertop Material For A Busy Kitchen?


For a household that cooks daily, hosts often, or has young kids, quartz is usually the most forgiving material. It's non-porous, stain-resistant, and never needs sealing. Granite is a close second and gives you a more natural look, but it does need periodic sealing. Marble is beautiful but high-maintenance, and we steer most busy kitchens away from it.

Can You Replace Just The Countertops Without Remodeling The Whole Kitchen?


No. C&S includes countertops as part of larger kitchen remodeling projects and doesn't take countertop-only replacement jobs. For a standalone replacement, contact a countertop fabricator. For a larger kitchen remodel, schedule a consultation to discuss the full scope.

What's The Difference Between Quartz And Quartzite?


Quartz is engineered (crushed natural quartz crystals bonded with resin) and is fully non-porous. Quartzite is a natural stone, harder than granite, with dramatic veining that resembles marble. Quartz is more uniform and lower maintenance; quartzite is more dramatic and a step up in price. We'll show you side-by-side samples during your consultation.

Will My New Countertops Match My Existing Cabinets And Floors?


That's exactly what the 3D rendering is for. Before fabrication, we render your full kitchen (countertops, cabinets, flooring, lighting) so you can see how the colors and textures work together. If something clashes, we change the material selection at that stage, not after installation.

Do You Offer Financing For Kitchen Countertops?


We can connect you with financing options during your consultation. Most San Antonio homeowners we work with use a combination of cash and home equity, but for projects in the higher range, financing through one of our partners is straightforward.

Kitchen Tile Installation In San Antonio

Custom kitchen tile installation in San Antonio, designed and installed by a veteran- and woman-owned remodeling team. C&S Remodeling has been remodeling kitchens across San Antonio and the Hill Country since 2015. We handle every step in-house: design, demolition, surface prep, and tile installation. The finished work matches the renderings you approved on day one.

Statement backsplashes, accent walls, and new floor tile that holds up to a busy household: our kitchen tile installers bring military precision and design-first thinking to every project. We start with complimentary 3D renderings, walk you through tile, grout, and pattern options, and stay involved through final cleanup.

CONTACT US
About Our Kitchen Tile Services

A well-installed tile job is the difference between a kitchen you love for fifteen years and one you redo in five. Tile sits at every wear point in the room: water at the sink, grease behind the range, foot traffic at the island. The installation has to be dialed in or it shows quickly. Lippage, hollow spots, uneven grout lines, and misaligned patterns are the most common reasons homeowners call us to redo someone else's work.

We install kitchen tile across three applications: backsplashes, accent walls, and floors. The same in-house crew that handles your demolition, plumbing, electrical, and finish work also lays the tile. Because we control every phase of the remodel, your tile installer isn't waiting on a subcontractor to finish before they can start, and you're not coordinating four trades yourself. Most kitchen tile jobs in San Antonio finish in three to seven working days once we mobilize, depending on square footage and pattern complexity.

You'll see the layout before we cut a single tile. We dry-lay the first row, walk you through grout color options against your cabinets and countertops, and confirm the pattern direction in person. That extra hour up front prevents the most common surprise homeowners face on tile projects: "I didn't realize it would look like that."

Different Types Of Kitchen Tilework
Custom Backsplash

The backsplash is the most photographed surface in any kitchen remodel. It sits at eye level, catches the light from your under-cabinet fixtures, and ties together the cabinets, countertop, and hood. We install kitchen backsplashes in San Antonio using ceramic, porcelain, glass, natural stone, and handmade tile, and we have layouts ready for whatever direction you want to go.

‍

Subway tile in standard or elongated sizes for a clean look that pairs with shaker or flat-panel cabinets. We can lay it straight stack, offset, herringbone, or vertical depending on the ceiling height and visual weight you're after.

‍

Mosaic and patterned tile for kitchens where the backsplash carries the personality of the room. Penny rounds, fish-scale, hexagon, encaustic-look porcelain, or decorative centerpieces above the range.

‍

Natural stone including marble, travertine, and slate when you want texture and depth. We seal stone properly and walk you through the maintenance trade-offs before installation, because not every stone belongs behind a stove.

‍

Glass and metal accents for transitional and contemporary kitchens, usually as part of a larger ceramic or porcelain field rather than the entire surface.

‍

We carry the backsplash up to the underside of the cabinets as standard, and we can take it to the ceiling on the range wall for a high-impact focal point. Outlets are cut clean, plug colors are matched to the tile, and finishing trims (Schluter, bullnose, pencil rail) are selected to suit the style. Nothing left raw or improvised.

Tile Wall Designs

Tile isn't just for the wall behind the range. Full accent walls have become one of the most-requested features in San Antonio kitchen remodels over the last two years, especially in open-concept floor plans where the kitchen is visible from the living area.

‍

We install full-height accent walls behind the range, on the rear of an island, or as a feature wall in a banquette or breakfast nook. Common applications include:

‍

Floor-to-ceiling range walls in vertical-stack subway, fluted ceramic, or zellige to draw the eye up and make a tall ceiling feel intentional.
Island back panels finished in the same tile as the backsplash for a cohesive look from any angle in an open kitchen.
Breakfast-nook accent walls in handmade or textured tile to soften a dining banquette and define the space without a wall partition.

‍

Wall tile gets cut and finished differently than backsplash work. Corners, transitions to drywall, and reveals around windows or open shelving need to be planned before tile leaves the box. We map every cut on the layout sketch you approve, so you'll know exactly where the cut tiles fall and how the pattern resolves at the edges.

Kitchen Tile Flooring

Kitchen floors take more abuse than any other surface in your home: dropped pans, spilled liquid, rolling stools, dog claws, and the constant foot traffic between the fridge, sink, and range triangle. Tile is the most durable option for the way San Antonio families actually use their kitchens, and it stays cool underfoot during the long Hill Country summers.

‍

We install kitchen floor tile in three primary materials:

‍

Porcelain for high-traffic kitchens. Through-body porcelain hides chips and scratches, resists staining, and handles temperature swings without cracking. Large-format porcelain (12"×24" and up) is our most-installed kitchen floor material and the easiest to keep clean.
Ceramic when budget matters and the kitchen sees moderate traffic. Glazed ceramic gives you nearly the same visual range as porcelain at a lower per-square-foot cost.
Natural stone (travertine, slate, and limestone) when you want warmth and texture and you're committed to sealing the floor on schedule. We walk through the maintenance reality before you sign off.

‍

Every kitchen floor we install starts with a flatness check on the subfloor. If the substrate isn't within ANSI A108 tolerance for the tile size, we self-level before laying a single sheet of underlayment. Large-format tile lippage is one of the most common callbacks in this industry, and almost every case traces back to subfloor prep that got skipped.

‍

We lay floors in straight, offset, herringbone, or diagonal patterns. The tile can run under the toe-kick of new cabinets or stop at the cabinet face. Your call, and the answer affects the order of operations on a full kitchen remodel.

CONTACT US
Tile Materials We Install

The tile material drives almost every other decision on a kitchen project: pattern options, grout choice, sealing schedule, even how the room feels underfoot in winter. Here's a quick reference for the materials we install most often in San Antonio kitchens:

Porcelain


Dense and low water absorption. Best for floors and high-moisture backsplashes. Available in styles that mimic marble, concrete, or wood at a fraction of the upkeep.

Natural Stone


Marble, travertine, slate, and limestone bring depth and one-of-a-kind veining. Requires periodic sealing; we'll set the schedule with you and recommend products that work in the San Antonio climate.

Handmade And Zellige


Slight color and dimensional variation that gives a backsplash genuine character. We let clients know up front that "imperfection" is the point. Uniform tiles are the wrong call here.

Ceramic


Lighter and easier to cut than porcelain. Good fit for backsplashes and accent walls where heavy wear isn't a concern. Wider color and pattern range than porcelain on the budget end.

Glass


Reflective and easy to clean. Great for accent strips and contemporary kitchens. Cuts and finishes need to be planned carefully because glass shows every imperfection along an edge.

Mosaic And Decorative


Pre-mounted sheets in penny round, hex, fish-scale, herringbone, and custom patterns. Useful for niches, listellos, and small accent zones.

Our Kitchen Tilework Process

Kitchen tilework is part design decision, part technical install. The projects that go smoothly are the ones where both halves get the time they deserve before tools come out. Here's how we run a kitchen tile project from first call to final walkthrough:

1. Free In-Home Consultation


We measure the work area, talk through your goals, and review any inspiration photos or designs you've already saved. If your tile project is part of a larger kitchen remodel, we scope the whole job in this visit.

2. Design And 3D Rendering


Carol or one of our designers builds a 3D rendering of the finished space, included free on every C&S project. You see the tile, grout color, pattern, and surrounding finishes together before any material is ordered.

3. Material Selection.


We help you select tile, grout, and trim from local San Antonio suppliers. You can visit showrooms with us or work from samples we bring to your home, whichever fits your schedule.

4. Demolition And Substrate Prep


Existing tile, drywall, or subflooring comes out, and we level and waterproof the substrate to the tile manufacturer's spec. This is the step homeowners can't see in a finished photo, but it's the step that determines whether your tile is still flat in ten years.

5. Tile Installation


We dry-lay the first row, confirm the layout with you, then install. You'll see daily progress photos if you're not on-site.

6. Grouting And Sealing


Grout color is finalized against the installed tile (lighting changes everything), then we seal natural stone and finish trim work.

7. Final Walkthrough


We walk the finished room with you, make any punch-list adjustments, and hand off cleaning and maintenance instructions. Project closeout includes warranty paperwork and care guides for your specific tile and grout combination.

Veteran- and woman-owned, family-operated. Scott brings a military and IT background to project planning and crew management; Carol leads design and material selection. The two of them are personally involved in every project, not handed off to a salesperson and a subcontractor.

The goal is a kitchen you love long-term, not a sale this week.

Frequently Asked Questions
How Much Does Kitchen Tile Installation Cost In San Antonio?


Kitchen tile pricing depends on three things: tile material, square footage, and pattern complexity. As a general benchmark for the San Antonio market, expect $4–$15 per square foot for materials and $5–$12 per square foot for installation, with intricate patterns (herringbone, mosaic, custom layouts) sitting at the higher end. We provide a fixed-price estimate after the in-home consultation so there are no surprises mid-project.

How Long Does A Kitchen Tile Project Take?


Most kitchen tile-only projects finish in 3 to 7 working days from demolition to final grout. Backsplash-only jobs are typically 2 to 4 days. Floor installations run 4 to 7 days because of substrate prep and curing time. If your tile work is part of a full kitchen remodel, the tile timeline integrates into the overall project schedule.

What's The Difference Between Porcelain And Ceramic For A Kitchen?


Porcelain is denser, absorbs less water, and resists chips and stains better. That makes it the go-to choice for kitchen floors and any backsplash near a sink or range. Ceramic costs less and comes in a wider style range on the budget end, and it works well for accent walls or backsplashes in lower-moisture areas. We'll recommend the right one based on where the tile is going and how much wear it'll see.

Do I Need To Seal My Kitchen Tile?


Glazed ceramic and porcelain don't need sealing; the glaze is the seal. Natural stone (marble, travertine, slate, limestone) and unglazed tiles do need to be sealed, typically every 1–3 years depending on the stone. Grout almost always benefits from sealing regardless of the tile choice. We use a penetrating sealer on grout lines as part of project closeout.

Can You Install Tile Over Existing Tile?


In some cases, yes. But it's usually not the best call for a kitchen. Floor heights change at every transition, cabinet kicks no longer line up, and any cracks or hollow spots in the original install will telegraph through to the new tile. We almost always recommend removing old tile to the substrate, checking the subfloor, and starting clean. We'll tell you if your project is one of the rare cases where overlay is the right move.

Do You Offer Free Estimates?


Yes. The initial consultation, measurement, and project estimate are free, and the 3D rendering is included on every C&S project at no cost. There's no pressure to commit during the visit; we want you confident in the decision before any work starts.

Are You Licensed And Insured?


Yes. C&S Remodeling is licensed and insured to operate in San Antonio and the surrounding Hill Country counties. We carry general liability and workers' comp on our crews, and we provide certificates of insurance on request before the project starts.

Our Step-By-Step 3D Rendering Process
1. Initial Consultation & Assessment

Our process begins with an in-depth consultation to understand your vision, goals, and preferences. We'll discuss your desired layout, style, and any specific features you want to include in your 3D remodeling image or video. This allows us to customize the design to your unique needs.

2. Design & Conceptualization

After understanding your vision, we begin creating 2D plans that outline the scope and structure of the remodel. These plans are an essential foundation, helping us explore potential design elements and allowing for further input from you before moving to the next step.

3. 3D Rendering Creation

Once the 2D plans are approved, we use advanced software to convert them into lifelike 3D models. This stage brings your project to life, showing you how your remodeled space will look and feel. You’ll be able to see every aspect of the design, from the placement of furniture and fixtures to the texture of materials and finishes.

4. Review & Revisions

We offer you the opportunity to review the 3D rendering in detail, giving you the flexibility to make adjustments. Whether you want to change the color of the walls, reposition cabinets, or explore different flooring options, we’re here to make those revisions. We offer up to 5 small revisions and 2 large revisions for free if requested within 30 days of delivering the initial results.

5. Final Approval

Once all revisions have been made and you’re happy with the design, we’ll seek your final approval. At this stage, the 3D rendering becomes the blueprint for the construction team, ensuring that your remodel is executed exactly as planned.

We also offer this service as a standalone option for homeowners who are planning future remodels but aren't quite ready to start construction. It's a great way to visualize potential ideas and make informed decisions without committing to a full project right away.

Should You Renovate Or Move?

San Antonio homeowners often face this decision: invest in renovating their current home or purchase a new one. Here's how to think through this choice:

‍

Consider Renovating If:
You love your location — Your neighborhood, schools, commute, and community connections are hard to replicate
Your home has good bones — Solid foundation, adequate square footage, and a layout that can be improved
Moving costs are prohibitive — Real estate commissions, closing costs, and moving expenses add up quickly
You want customization — Building exactly what you want is easier through renovation than finding a perfect existing home
You have equity to leverage — Home equity can fund renovations at lower interest rates than new mortgages
Consider Moving If:
Your home is fundamentally too small — Adding square footage through additions is expensive and not always possible
Location no longer works — Job changes, school needs, or lifestyle shifts may require a new area
Structural issues are severe — Foundation problems or outdated systems may cost more to fix than the home is worth
The market favors selling — Strong seller's markets can make moving financially attractive

‍

The Numbers

In San Antonio, selling a home and purchasing another typically costs 8-12% of the home's value in transaction fees alone, before considering the price difference between homes. A comprehensive renovation that transforms your existing home often delivers more value per dollar while letting you stay in a location you love.

What To Expect: Whole Home Remodel Timeline
Phase 1: Design & Planning (4-8 Weeks)

We begin with in-depth consultations to understand your vision, lifestyle, and budget. Our team creates detailed plans, 3D renderings, and material selections. This phase includes permit applications and contractor scheduling. Taking time here prevents costly changes during construction.

Phase 2: Demolition & Structural Work (2-4 Weeks)

Selective demolition removes outdated elements while preserving what stays. Any structural modifications—wall removals, beam installations, foundation work—happen during this phase. We also address hidden issues like outdated wiring or plumbing discovered during demo.

Phase 3: Rough-In Work (3-6 Weeks)

Behind-the-walls work includes electrical rewiring, plumbing relocations, HVAC modifications, and insulation upgrades. Smart home infrastructure is installed during this phase. Inspections verify code compliance before walls close.

Phase 4: Finishing Work (6-12 Weeks)

The transformation becomes visible: drywall, trim, cabinetry, flooring, tile, paint, fixtures, and appliances. This phase takes the most time because each room moves through multiple trades in sequence.

Phase 5: Final Details (1-2 Weeks)

Touch-ups, final inspections, hardware installation, cleaning, and quality walkthrough. We don't consider a project complete until you're delighted with every detail.

Total Timeline: 4-8 Months

Most comprehensive whole-home renovations in San Antonio take 4-8 months from design through completion. Your project manager provides a detailed schedule during planning so you can make appropriate living arrangements.

Frequently Asked Questions About Whole Home Remodeling
Can I Live In My Home During A Whole-House Renovation?


It depends on the scope. Minor renovations may allow you to stay by working room-by-room. Comprehensive renovations that affect multiple systems simultaneously typically require temporary housing for 2-4 months. We'll discuss this during planning and help you make appropriate arrangements.

Do I Need Permits For A Whole Home Remodel?


Yes. San Antonio requires permits for structural changes, electrical work, plumbing modifications, and HVAC updates. We handle all permit applications and inspections as part of our full-service approach, ensuring your renovation meets code and is properly documented for future resale.

How Do You Protect Areas Not Being Renovated?


We install plastic barriers, floor protection, and air filtration systems to contain dust and debris. Areas completed early receive protective coverings until the entire project finishes. Our crews clean daily to maintain a safe, organized job site.

What's The Return On Investment For A Whole Home Remodel?


While ROI varies by project, comprehensive renovations in San Antonio typically recoup 50-70% of investment at resale. More importantly, you'll enjoy a home customized to your needs for years before any potential sale. The daily quality-of-life improvement often outweighs financial calculations.

Can You Work With My Existing Floor Plan Or Do I Need An Architect?


Our design-build approach includes experienced designers who can optimize your existing floor plan without hiring a separate architect for most projects. For major structural changes or additions, we collaborate with licensed architects and include that coordination in our services.

What If We Discover Hidden Problems During Renovation?


It happens—older homes especially may have hidden wiring issues, plumbing problems, or structural concerns not visible until demolition. We maintain contingency allowances in budgets and communicate immediately when discoveries occur, presenting options before proceeding.

Bring Your Dream Home To Life With 3d Rendering Services

we offer cutting-edge 3D renderings to help you visualize the project you have in mind, or before construction begins on your home remodel. Our 3D visualizations allow you to explore design options, make adjustments, and confidently plan your project with precision and clarity. Ready to see your dream space come to life? Contact us today to schedule a consultation and start planning your remodel with a clear vision!

CONTACT US
3D House Renderings
Visualize Your Dream Space

In the world of home remodeling, 3D renderings have revolutionized how homeowners and contractors plan, design, and visualize projects. A 3D rendering is a digital representation, or visual 3D of a space, created using specialized software that transforms a 2D design into a lifelike, three-dimensional image. It allows homeowners to see an accurate portrayal of what their remodel will look like before any physical work begins.

Home Remodeling Benefits

Using 3D renderings in home remodeling offers several key benefits. First, it provides a realistic preview of your home transformation, enabling you to visualize design choices such as layout, colors, materials, and finishes in great detail. This 3D visualizer helps ensure that you're confident in your decisions before construction begins, eliminating guesswork and costly last-minute changes.

A Shared Vision

Your data privacy and home security are top priorities for us. We use smart home systems with robust encryption and advanced security protocols to protect against unauthorized access, ensuring that your smart home remains secure and your personal information is protected at all times.

Realistic 3D Visualization For Potential Remodels

One of the most significant advantages of 3D renderings is the ability to see your project in highly detailed, realistic visual 3D. Whether you're planning a kitchen renovation, bathroom remodel, or a full home makeover, a project rendering will show you exactly what your finished space will look like, down to the smallest details. This advanced technology offers a far more accurate picture than traditional blueprints or sketches.

Our Testimonials
Realistic 3D Visualization For Potential Remodels

Because you can visualize the space so clearly, three-dimensional images allow you to make changes early in the design phase, before construction starts. Whether you want to adjust a layout, swap out materials, or change a color scheme, these decisions can be made effortlessly within the 3D-rendered software. This saves both time and money, as it reduces the need for costly changes during the construction phase.

Enhanced Communication Between Homeowners & Contractors

A 3D rendering ensures that both you and your contractor have a shared understanding of the project. These visuals act as a guide throughout the remodel, ensuring clarity in decision-making and execution. This streamlines the communication process and eliminates the potential for misinterpretation, leading to smoother, more efficient projects.

Are You Ready To Create Your New Space?
Book Appointment
Our Step-By-Step 3D Rendering Process
1. Initial Consultation & Assessment

Our process begins with an in-depth consultation to understand your vision, goals, and preferences. We'll discuss your desired layout, style, and any specific features you want to include in your 3D remodeling image or video. This allows us to customize the design to your unique needs.

2. Design & Conceptualization

After understanding your vision, we begin creating 2D plans that outline the scope and structure of the remodel. These plans are an essential foundation, helping us explore potential design elements and allowing for further input from you before moving to the next step.

3. 3D Rendering Creation

Once the 2D plans are approved, we use advanced software to convert them into lifelike 3D models. This stage brings your project to life, showing you how your remodeled space will look and feel. You’ll be able to see every aspect of the design, from the placement of furniture and fixtures to the texture of materials and finishes.

4. Review & Revisions

We offer you the opportunity to review the 3D rendering in detail, giving you the flexibility to make adjustments. Whether you want to change the color of the walls, reposition cabinets, or explore different flooring options, we’re here to make those revisions. We offer up to 5 small revisions and 2 large revisions for free if requested within 30 days of delivering the initial results.

5. Final Approval

Once all revisions have been made and you’re happy with the design, we’ll seek your final approval. At this stage, the 3D rendering becomes the blueprint for the construction team, ensuring that your remodel is executed exactly as planned.

We also offer this service as a standalone option for homeowners who are planning future remodels but aren't quite ready to start construction. It's a great way to visualize potential ideas and make informed decisions without committing to a full project right away.

What You Can Customize In Your 3D Rendering

One of the biggest advantages of 3D renderings is the level of customization they offer. At C&S Remodeling, the possibilities are endless when it comes to designing your dream space. Here’s a glimpse of what you can personalize:

Interior 3D Rendering Features

Flooring:

Choose from hardwood, tile, carpet, or other materials to match your design preferences and the specific needs of each room.

‍

Cabinetry:

Select custom cabinetry styles, colors, and finishes to reflect your taste and enhance storage in kitchens, bathrooms, or other spaces.

‍

Fixtures:

Experiment with a variety of lighting fixtures, faucets, and hardware to personalize the look and functionality of your home.

‍

Wall Colors:

Explore a range of paint shades and wall treatments, including accent walls or textured finishes, to refresh and modernize your space.

‍

Choose from materials like granite, quartz, marble, or laminate for durable and stylish countertops, with options to customize edges and finishes.

‍

Backsplashes:

Experiment with different backsplash materials, patterns, and colors in the kitchen or bathroom, such as tile, glass, or stone for a unique touch.

‍

Room Additions:

Add new rooms like a home office, sunroom, or additional living space to improve the flow and functionality of your home.

‍

Windows & Doors:

Upgrade to new window and door designs with energy-efficient models, custom frame materials, and different sizes or shapes to enhance both style and performance.

‍

Open Floor Plans:

Create an open, airy layout by removing walls or adding design features like arches, optimizing space and light in common areas.

‍

Kitchen & Bathroom Remodels:

Redesign these essential spaces with new layouts, updated cabinetry, modern fixtures, and upgraded surfaces like countertops and backsplashes for a fresh, functional look.

Exterior 3D Rendering Features

Window & Door Design:

Preview new window and door styles, sizes, and materials to ensure they enhance the architecture and overall curb appeal of your remodel.

‍

Exterior Facade Upgrades:

Experiment with adding stone accents, modern trim, or updated siding to completely transform your home’s appearance.

‍

Porch & Patio Additions:

Visualize updates or expansions to porches and patios, ensuring they seamlessly integrate with the exterior design.

‍

Garage Remodels:

Explore design changes for your garage, including new doors, finishes, and materials, to create a more cohesive exterior.

‍

Entryway Enhancements:

Preview new front doors, steps, or columns to enhance your entryway and make a bold statement in your exterior remodel.

‍

Additional 3D Rendering Services

Aerial Renderings:

Capture a bird’s-eye view of your project with detailed aerial renderings, offering a full perspective of your property or construction site from above.

‍

3D Animations:

Bring your project to life with dynamic 3D animations that provide a walk-through experience, showcasing every detail and design element in motion.

‍

Virtual Reality Tours:

Immerse yourself in a fully interactive 3D environment with virtual reality tours, allowing you to explore and experience your future space in real time.

‍

360 Panoramas:

Get a comprehensive view of your project with 360-degree panoramic renderings, offering an ultra-high-definition, all-encompassing look at your entire space.

‍

Whatever your vision, our 3D renderings allow you to customize every detail to create the perfect space for your home.

Why 3D Rendering Transforms The Remodeling Experience

Traditional blueprints and 2D sketches leave too much to imagination. Our 3D home renderings show you what the finished project will actually look like, so you can make decisions you feel good about.

‍

Eliminate Costly Surprises

The average homeowner makes 3-5 design changes during construction, and each one can add thousands to the final cost. With photorealistic 3D renderings, you can experiment with layouts, materials, and colors before construction starts. That cuts out most of those expensive mid-project changes.

‍

Make Confident Material Selections

Choosing between quartz and granite countertops? Wondering how that bold tile pattern will look in your bathroom? Our renderings show you exactly how different materials, finishes, and fixtures will appear in your actual space, under your actual lighting conditions.

‍

Align Family Expectations

Getting everyone on the same page is easier when everyone can see the same vision. Share your 3D renderings with family members so everyone agrees on the direction before work starts.

3D Rendering FAQ
What Are 3D Renders?


3D renders or 3D rendering is the process of creating a digital, three-dimensional image or video of a space. When an area is 3D-rendered you can visualize a potential remodel before construction begins.

How Much Do 3D Renderings Cost?


At C&S Remodeling 3D renderings are included as part of the remodeling package. However, they are also available as a standalone service without committing to a remodel if you have a future project in mind. Prices vary based on the scope of the project (e.g., kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, or whole home remodeling) and how soon you need the rendering.

What Is The Turnaround Time For A 3D Rendering?


The turnaround time for a 3D rendering typically ranges from 24 hours to 14 business days, depending on the complexity and scope of the project. Factors such as design intricacy, revisions, and project size can influence the delivery time.

How Many 3D-Rendered Revisions Are Included?


We offer up to 5 small revisions and 2 large revisions for free if requested within 30 days of delivering the initial results. Additional revisions or requests made after the 30-day period will incur extra costs.

How Accurate Is The Final Project Compared To The 3D Rendering?


The final project is highly accurate compared to the 3D rendering, as we use the renderings as a detailed blueprint throughout the construction process. This ensures that the finished remodel closely aligns with the original design, allowing for minimal deviations and a precise execution of your vision.

What Is The Difference Between Regular 3D Renderings & Architectural Renderings?


Architectural floor plans are technical drawings focused on the precise layout and structure of a building, including measurements and compliance with regulations. In contrast, regular 3D renderings are visual representations that focus on aesthetics, showing how a space will look with materials, lighting, and furniture. While floor plans guide construction, 3D renderings provide a realistic view for design decisions and presentations.

Home & Room Additions In San Antonio, TX

C&S Remodeling is a veteran-owned and woman-owned design-build company creating home and room additions for San Antonio homeowners.

A room addition should fix something that no longer works in the current floor plan. It may give a growing family another bedroom, create a private suite for a parent, open up a crowded kitchen, or add a comfortable place to gather. Our team helps you shape the footprint and layout around that need, then choose finishes that make sense beside the existing rooms. We handle design, construction, plumbing, and electrical as one coordinated project. Complimentary 3D renderings let you see the proposed space before work begins.

CONTACT US
Our Home Addition Services

Room additions can take many forms, but the right plan starts with the way your household needs to use the space. Some projects add a single focused room. Others rework part of the existing floor plan so the new square footage improves the whole home instead of creating an isolated wing.

C&S Remodeling plans home additions around those everyday needs. We start with the available footprint and the path people will take through the new layout. Privacy, daylight, and storage come next, along with the relationship between the addition and the rooms beside it. Exterior proportions and finish transitions matter too; the addition has to work from the street as well as from the inside.

Our design-build approach keeps those decisions connected. The people discussing the layout also understand what it will take to build, wire, plumb, and finish the space. Complimentary 3D rendering help you compare options and make selections with a clearer picture of the finished addition.

Bedroom Addition


An extra bedroom can support a growing household, frequent guests, or a family member who needs more privacy. Furniture placement comes first. From there, we plan closets, windows, and the connection to a nearby bathroom or hallway so the room feels like part of the original layout.

Kitchen Additions And Expansions


When the existing kitchen footprint can't support better flow, more storage, or the gathering space a family wants, expanding outward may be the practical answer. The added square footage can make room for an island, pantry, dining area, or a less crowded work triangle. Because C&S also handles kitchen remodeling, we can plan the expansion and the interior kitchen as one project.

Sunrooms And Flexible-Use Rooms


A bright room can serve as a reading space, hobby room, playroom, studio, or relaxed place to host friends. Orientation, shade, windows, flooring, and heating or cooling choices all affect how comfortable the room will be throughout the year, so those decisions belong in the plan from the start.

Garages And Practical Storage Spaces


A garage addition can create protected parking, workshop room, household storage, or a better transition into the home. We plan it around vehicle clearance, doors, storage zones, and how the exterior mass relates to the house. A smaller dedicated storage or hobby structure can solve a different need without taking over a bedroom or living area.

Shed Addition


Create a dedicated space for storage, hobbies, woodworking, DIY projects, and more. Instead of cluttered, multi-use spaces inside your home, you can unlock a new, separate area.

Primary Suites And In-Law Suites


A private suite may combine a bedroom, bathroom, storage, and a small sitting area. For extended-family living, the priorities may also include a more independent entrance, convenient access through the home, and a layout that respects everyone's routines. We use the design phase to balance privacy with connection.

Family Rooms And Living Rooms


A larger gathering space can change how the entire home feels. We consider seating and media needs, then look at views and traffic between the kitchen, patio, and bedrooms. More square footage only helps when the room has a clear purpose.

Bathrooms


A bathroom addition may support a new bedroom suite, reduce competition in a busy household, or make the home's layout more practical for guests. Plumbing locations, storage, ventilation, privacy, and finish selections all need to work together. Our bathroom remodeling and design-build team coordinates those pieces with the surrounding construction.

Second-Story And Multi-Room Additions


Larger additions can create several rooms or add space where the lot offers limited room to expand outward. These projects call for especially careful planning around stairs, structure, rooflines, and the relationship between new and existing systems. C&S helps homeowners explore the layout in 3D before settling on the direction.

Tiny Home Designs


Our tiny home designs combine functionality and style, maximizing every square foot to create efficient, comfortable, and inviting living spaces.

Why San Antonio Homeowners Choose C&S Remodeling

A home addition is a major change to a place you already know well. You need a team that can listen to what works, recognize what doesn't, and carry the design through construction without losing the original idea along the way.

‍

Veteran-owned, woman-owned, and family-run. Scott and Carol Kressner founded C&S Remodeling in 2015. Their backgrounds bring project discipline and design perspective to the same table, and both remain personally involved in the business and its projects.

‍

One design-build team. C&S handles design, construction, plumbing, and electrical through one company. Layout decisions stay tied to the practical details of building the addition, and homeowners work with the same team throughout the project.

‍

Complimentary 3D renderings. Floor plans can be hard to picture when walls, rooflines, and existing rooms are all changing. C&S includes 3D renderings with projects so you can understand the proposed layout and make design decisions with a visual reference.

‍

A focus on fit. A well-planned home addition doesn't call attention to the line between old and new. We consider the room connections, material transitions, and the relationship between the addition and the current exterior. The finished space should look at home there.

‍

Local experience. C&S serves San Antonio and surrounding communities including Alamo Heights, Boerne, Bulverde, Fair Oaks Ranch, Helotes, New Braunfels, Shavano Park, and Timberwood Park. That local focus keeps the work grounded in the homes and lifestyles found across the area. Homeowners can also browse C&S's broader remodeling portfolio while verified addition-specific case studies are prepared for this page.

Our Testimonials

Book Appointment
Our Home Addition Process

A room addition affects more than one part of a home. The layout has to work with the exterior design. Plumbing and electrical decisions have to fit the plan, and the finish selections need to be ready when construction calls for them. C&S keeps those conversations together through its design-build process.

1. Free Consultation

We start with the reason you want more space. You'll walk us through the home, explain what isn't working, and share any ideas, photos, or priorities you already have. We use that conversation to understand the project goals and identify the questions the design needs to answer.

2. Existing-Home Review

The team studies the current floor plan and the likely connection points. We also look at the way the property can support an addition, then discuss neighboring rooms, circulation, natural light, exterior proportions, and the household's routines during construction.

3. Design And Complimentary 3D Renderings

C&S develops a layout that gives the new space a clear function while connecting it to the rest of the home. Complimentary 3D renderings make the proposal easier to evaluate. You can see room relationships, key finishes, and design details before the project moves ahead.

4. Scope And Selections

Once the direction is clear, the team works through the construction scope and the material choices that shape the final result. Early decisions about flooring, cabinetry, fixtures, lighting, windows, doors, and exterior finishes help reduce guesswork once work is underway.

5. Construction And Communication

C&S coordinates design, construction, plumbing, and electrical through one company. The team keeps the approved plan at the center of the work and communicates as the addition takes shape.

6. Final Walkthrough

At the end of the project, we review the completed space with you and address the final details. The finished addition should support the need that started the project and feel at home beside the rooms that were already there.

Designing An Addition That Belongs

An addition can meet every square-foot requirement and still feel wrong if the connection to the original house is awkward. Good design looks at the whole composition. The new room needs a comfortable path from the existing floor plan, sensible proportions, and a clear reason for where doors, windows, storage, and furniture will go.

‍

Exterior decisions matter just as much. Roof shape, window rhythm, siding, masonry, trim, and the overall mass of the addition affect how natural it looks from the street and yard. Exact material matches aren't always available, especially as homes age, so the plan may call for a deliberate transition rather than a forced imitation.

‍

Inside, continuity doesn't require every surface to match. Flooring may carry through, or a clear threshold may mark the change. Trim and ceiling heights can connect the spaces while lighting, paint, cabinetry, and hardware give the new room its own character.

‍

Complimentary 3D renderings give you a practical way to review those relationships. You'll be able to see how the addition sits beside the existing home and how key interior elements work together before committing to the final direction. That early clarity helps the finished space feel planned from the beginning.

When To Consider A Home Addition

An addition makes sense when you like your home and location but the existing footprint no longer supports the way you live. That tension often shows up gradually: a dining table becomes a work desk, guests sleep in a multipurpose room, storage spills into living areas, or a family member needs privacy the current floor plan can't provide.

‍

Common reasons San Antonio homeowners explore room additions include:

‍

A household is growing or changing. A new bedroom, bathroom, or suite can create room for children, guests, or extended family without forcing the household into a move.
The kitchen or living area is too tight. Expanding a high-use space can improve circulation, storage, seating, and the connection between cooking and gathering areas.
Work or hobbies need a dedicated room. A home office, studio, workshop, or flexible room can keep focused activities from taking over bedrooms and common areas.
The home needs a better long-term fit. A thoughtfully located suite or first-floor room can support new routines and give the family more options as needs change.
The property works, but the floor plan doesn't. If you value the neighborhood, yard, schools, and community, adding the right space may be preferable to starting over elsewhere.

More square footage isn't automatically the right answer. A better interior layout may solve the problem inside the current footprint. In other cases, the home simply needs more room. C&S can compare both directions during the consultation and help you decide which one fits the house and your priorities.

Home Addition Costs In San Antonio

The cost of a home addition in San Antonio depends on what you're adding and how the new construction connects to the existing house. A simple-looking room can involve foundation, structure, roofing, windows, insulation, electrical work, interior finishes, and changes to adjacent spaces. Add a kitchen or bathroom, and plumbing, cabinetry, fixtures, tile, and appliances may become part of the scope as well.

‍

The biggest cost drivers usually include:

‍

Size and room type. Bedrooms, living rooms, kitchens, bathrooms, garages, and multi-room suites each call for different systems and finishes.
Connection to the existing home. Opening walls, tying into a roofline, extending utilities, and blending floor levels can affect the work required.
Structural and site conditions. The location of the addition, access to the work area, and the way the existing house is built all influence the plan.
Finish selections. Flooring, cabinetry, countertops, windows, doors, lighting, plumbing fixtures, and exterior materials can move a project in very different directions.
Work inside the existing footprint. An addition often changes the room beside it. Reworking a kitchen, hallway, bathroom, or living area may be necessary to make the expanded plan function well.

Use $250 to $400 per square foot as a starting range for a finished room addition. C&S then prices your project from its design and scope.

During the planning process, you'll be able to see how the layout and selections affect the project before construction begins. Schedule Your Free Consultation to start with the space, priorities, and investment level you have in mind.

Read the room addition cost guide for planning ranges by room type.

Plan Your San Antonio Room Addition

Start with what the home needs to do better. Who will use the new space? What will happen there every day, and which nearby rooms may need to change? Those answers are more useful at the beginning than a finish list or a guessed room size.

Bring those ideas to C&S Remodeling, even if they're still rough. Scott, Carol, and the design-build team can help you compare layouts, understand the decisions ahead, and shape a room addition that works with the home you already have. You'll also receive complimentary 3D renderings with the project so the plan is easier to understand before construction.

Frequently Asked Questions
What Kinds Of Room Additions Does C&S Remodeling Design And Build?


C&S works on bedrooms, bathrooms, primary suites, in-law suites, kitchen expansions, family rooms, living rooms, sunrooms, garages, and larger multi-room additions. The right option depends on the need you're trying to solve and the way the new space will connect to the existing home.

Can You Expand My Kitchen As Part Of A Home Addition?


Yes. C&S can plan the added square footage and the kitchen remodel as one connected project. That lets the team coordinate layout, cabinetry, plumbing, electrical work, lighting, storage, and the transition into nearby dining or living spaces.

Will The Addition Match My Existing Home?


Matching the character of the existing house is a central design goal. C&S looks at rooflines, exterior materials, windows, trim, floor levels, interior finishes, and circulation so the new space feels related to the original home. When an exact material match isn't practical, the team can plan a transition that still looks intentional.

Do Home Addition Projects Include 3D Renderings?


Yes. Complimentary 3D renderings are included with C&S projects. They show the proposed room relationships and design details before construction, making it easier to compare options and give specific feedback.

How Do I Decide Between Remodeling And Adding Space?


Start with the problem the current floor plan creates. If a better layout can solve it within the existing footprint, remodeling may be the more focused approach. If the home truly lacks the square footage for another bedroom, suite, larger kitchen, or gathering room, an addition may give you more useful options. C&S can discuss both directions during the consultation.

What Affects The Cost Of A Room Addition In San Antonio?


Size, room type, structural conditions, roof and utility connections, access, finish selections, and changes inside the existing home all affect cost. A bathroom or kitchen addition also brings different plumbing, cabinetry, fixture, and surface needs than a bedroom or living area. C&S prices the work from the actual design and project scope.

How Does The C&S Design-Build Process Help With An Addition?


Design, construction, plumbing, and electrical stay connected through one company. That means design choices can be reviewed alongside the work required to build them, and homeowners aren't left coordinating separate teams. Scott and Carol Kressner also bring the family's project and design perspectives into the process.

Where Does C&S Remodeling Build Home Additions?


C&S serves San Antonio and nearby Hill Country communities, including Alamo Heights, Boerne, Bulverde, Fair Oaks Ranch, Helotes, New Braunfels, Shavano Park, and Timberwood Park. Contact the team to discuss your address and the addition you have in mind.
